title: Immune and inflammatory features associated with pyroptosis- and myocardial fibrosis-related genes in HFpEF: a machine learning study
summary: Machine-learning feature selection from transcriptomic data proposed a three-gene HFpEF signature; a small clinical cohort linked one marker with HFpEF status and clinical measurements. Results are exploratory: the signature was unstable across resampling, cross-species expression directions differed, and the evidence does not establish causal mechanisms or clinical biomarkers.
ai_technology: Machine-learning feature selection prioritized candidate genes and fit an exploratory transcriptomic classifier.
organization: Not stated in the reviewed publisher full text

evidence.tested: A three-gene signature was proposed; lower whole-blood PTPN11 was associated with HFpEF status and higher NT-proBNP/CRP in a small clinical cohort.
evidence.unknown: The exact gene set showed limited resampling stability; the clinical cohort was small and unmatched, with no causal or clinical diagnostic evidence.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning feature selection generated candidate signature findings from transcriptomic cohorts.

source_review.scope: Primary source full-text Methods and Results; version date and reported validation scope checked.
